name: Microsoft Xbox One family
summary: Explore the Xbox One family — the 2013 original, the One S and the One X. There is no retail-mode homebrew route comparable to the 360's RGH or the original Xbox's softmod; the documented path is Microsoft's own Developer Mode, plus research-level privilege escalation inside it.

specs.storage: Internal hard drive, model-dependent; external USB storage supported
specs.media: Blu-ray drive; 4K UHD Blu-ray on the One S and One X
specs.display: 1080p (One); 4K upscaling and HDR10 (One S); native 4K (One X)

variants.notes: Launch 2013-11-22 (NA/EU), 2014-09-04 (Japan). External power supply, Kinect port. All three models run the same system software and take the same Developer Mode activation.

variants.storage: 500 GB, 1 TB or 2 TB hard drive
variants.notes: Adds 4K video output and upscaling, HDR10 support. Smaller case, internal power supply, no Kinect port. Does not provide native 4K game rendering.
Mid-generation performance model. Native 4K game rendering. All three models run the same system software line.

firmware.version: Microsoft system software, updated online with preview/insider rings

homebrew.name: Developer Mode
homebrew.firmware: All firmware versions; entered through the Dev Mode app
homebrew.summary: Microsoft's sanctioned development environment for retail Xbox One consoles. It runs UWP apps including homebrew apps and emulators packaged for the console. It needs a Microsoft account and the Dev Mode activation; it does not give kernel-level control of the retail OS.

compatibility.note: Model does not change eligibility. All three models take the same Developer Mode activation per Microsoft.

requirements: A Microsoft account and the Dev Mode app from the store.
warnings: Developer Mode is not a jailbreak. It is a Microsoft-provided environment with its own limits.

homebrew.name: Security research (privilege escalation, browser issues)
homebrew.summary: The Xbox One Research Wiki catalogues exploits such as Developer Mode privilege escalation and browser-based issues. These are security research, not a maintained CFW path.

compatibility.note: Research-only; no public retail exploit route is documented.

warnings: Not a user route. No custom firmware or NAND-based CFW project is documented.

homebrew.name: Xbox One offline system update (OSU)
homebrew.summary: Microsoft's USB-based update and recovery for a console that will not boot. It reinstalls the system software and keeps or erases data depending on the option chosen.

compatibility.note: Official recovery track shared by the whole family.

requirements: USB drive with the official OSU file.
warnings: Switching back to Retail Mode and removing the Dev Mode storage returns the console to a normal state.

officialSupport.summary: Xbox One remains supported; Developer Mode is active for all models.
